steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement that imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState from 'react'. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs to bring in both React and useState from 'react'. Make sure you're using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the useFeatureFlag hook function
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function named 'useFeatureFlag' that returns a boolean value. Use TypeScript syntax and define it after the imports.
steps.hint: Define a function called useFeatureFlag that returns a boolean (e.g., true or false). You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the useFeatureFlag hook function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook function named useFeatureFlag is defined, returning a boolean value.
successCriteria: Uses TypeScript syntax (explicit return type or inference)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useFeatureFlag hook function with proper TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named exactly 'useFeatureFlag' and returns a boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named 'useFeatureFlag' that returns a boolean.

steps.title: Add parameters to the hook with TypeScript interface
steps.instruction: Add a parameter to the useFeatureFlag hook function and define its type using a TypeScript interface. The interface should be named FeatureFlagConfig and include a property 'flagName' of type string.
steps.hint: Define an interface first, then add it as the type for the hook's parameter. Remember to use proper TypeScript syntax with a colon.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFeatureFlag hook should accept a typed parameter using the FeatureFlagConfig interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a TypeScript interface for the hook parameters and added it to the useFeatureFlag function. This provides type safety for the feature flag configuration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined the FeatureFlagConfig interface with a 'flagName' property of type string, and added it as the parameter type for useFeatureFlag.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook still needs a typed parameter. Define a FeatureFlagConfig interface with 'flagName: string', then add it as the parameter type to useFeatureFlag.

steps.title: Initialize state for feature flag status
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag hook, add a useState hook to track whether the feature is enabled. Initialize it with false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to specify the type as boolean.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with useState
const [isEnabled, setIsEnabled] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFeatureFlag hook now has a state variable to track the feature flag's enabled status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the state for tracking the feature flag status. The useState hook with boolean type and false initial value is correctly set up.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check if you've included all required elements: useState with boolean type, initialized to false, with proper variable names (isEnabled/setIsEnabled).
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. You need to add a useState hook inside the useFeatureFlag function to track whether the feature is enabled, initialized to false with boolean type.

steps.title: Add useEffect to simulate API call
steps.instruction: Import the useEffect hook from 'react' and add it inside your useFeatureFlag hook to simulate fetching the feature flag status from an API.
steps.hint: Add the import statement for useEffect, then call useEffect inside your hook function with a callback that contains your simulation logic.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is imported and added to the useFeatureFlag hook with a simulation of fetching feature flag status.
successCriteria: Add useEffect call inside useFeatureFlag hook
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported useEffect and added it to simulate an API call. This will allow your hook to fetch the feature flag status when the component mounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some missing pieces. Make sure you've imported useEffect from 'react' and added it inside your useFeatureFlag hook with a callback function and dependency array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't match what was requested. You need to import useEffect from 'react' and add it inside your useFeatureFlag hook to simulate fetching feature flag status.

steps.title: Implement mock API call logic
steps.instruction: Inside the useEffect hook, add a setTimeout function to simulate an API response delay. Set the timeout to 1000 milliseconds (1 second). Inside the timeout callback, call setFlagStatus with the value 'enabled' to simulate a successful API response.
steps.hint: Use setTimeout(() => { setFlagStatus('enabled'); }, 1000); inside your useEffect.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook now contains a setTimeout that will simulate an API response after 1 second, setting the flag status to 'enabled'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the mock API call logic. The setTimeout simulates a 1-second delay before setting the flag status to 'enabled', mimicking a real API response.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all the required elements: setTimeout with 1000ms delay, calling setFlagStatus('enabled') inside the timeout callback, and placing this inside the useEffect hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mock API call logic isn't implemented correctly. You need to add a setTimeout inside the useEffect that calls setFlagStatus('enabled') after 1000 milliseconds.

steps.title: Update state based on mock response
steps.instruction: Inside the useEffect, update the feature flag state to true when the mock API call resolves successfully.
steps.hint: After the setTimeout resolves, call setFlagEnabled with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect will now update the feature flag state to true after the mock API call completes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully updated the state when the mock API call completes. This simulates receiving a successful response from a feature flag service.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling setFlagEnabled with the value true inside the setTimeout callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state update is missing or incorrect. Inside the setTimeout callback, you need to call setFlagEnabled(true) to update the feature flag status.

steps.title: Return the feature flag state from hook
steps.instruction: Return the `isEnabled` state value from the `useFeatureFlag` hook function.
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, use a `return` statement to return the current value of `isEnabled`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now returns the current feature flag status, making it usable in components.
successCriteria: The `useFeatureFlag` function should end with a `return` statement that returns the `isEnabled` state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the feature flag state from your custom hook. This makes the hook usable in components where you can access the current flag status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the return statement might be missing or not returning the correct value. Make sure you're returning the `isEnabled` state variable directly from the hook function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook doesn't seem to return the feature flag state. Remember to add a `return` statement at the end of your `useFeatureFlag` function that returns the `isEnabled` variable.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element. The component should be defined after the useFeatureFlag hook.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns a JSX element like a div. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional App component is created with a return statement that outputs JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component. This is the main entry point for your React application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a component named App that returns JSX. Check that it's defined after the useFeatureFlag hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to define a function named App that returns JSX, and place it after the useFeatureFlag hook.

steps.title: Use the feature flag hook in App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, call the useFeatureFlag hook with a feature name string to get the feature flag status.
steps.hint: Call the hook like this: const isEnabled = useFeatureFlag('new-feature');
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will call the useFeatureFlag hook to retrieve the status of a specific feature flag.
successCriteria: useFeatureFlag hook is called inside App component
Hook is called with a string parameter representing a feature name
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the useFeatureFlag hook inside your App component. This allows the component to access the feature flag status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the useFeatureFlag hook with a feature name string parameter inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useFeatureFlag hook needs to be called inside the App component with a feature name string parameter.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component so it can be imported and used in other files.

steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported and ready to be imported elsewhere.
